newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy union opposes length of service pension cut.
newsitem.headline: Italy union opposes length of service pension cut.

text.p: The leader of Italy's UIL trade union confederation, Pietro Larizza, said on Monday he could not accept any cuts in length of service pensions or an extension of contributions in talks on reforming the unwieldy pension system.
"I'm waiting to hear exactly what the government puts forward," Larizza said in an interview with state radio Rai.
"If it should propose the abolition of length of service pensions and the extension of the contributions system, I exclude the possibility of a deal," he said.
Bilateral talks on pensions between the centre-left government and union leaders, employers' organisation Confindustria and other business groups were set to begin on Tuesday morning.
It will be the first time the thorny issue of pension reform has been addressed in detail since negotiations on streamlining the welfare state were launched a month ago.

Larizza said the government should differentiate clearly between social security and pensions. "We must know exactly the pensions system situation and not that of the social security system," he said.

Italy is under pressure to carry out a convincing reform of social spending and to shake up its pensions system to prove that public finances will be kept under control before the planned 1999 launch of the single European currency.
The talks, officially launched in June but which only got underway properly earlier this month, immediately ran into trouble over Italy's generous early retirement system.
The system allows Italians to draw a pension based on the length of service even before they have reach mandatory retirement age.

Trades unions agree that the welfare system should be changed, but they want reforms to focus on providing employment and unemployment benefits. They are staunchly against cuts in spending, especially for pensions.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi said in June that state spending on pensions is some 15 trillion lire a year over budget and needs bringing into line. The government says the aim is to rebalance spending, rather than implement cuts.
